population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling arithmetic: ever 16.5% − current 9.9% = 6.6% of adults have used and are off now; about half of current users (≈5.0 pts) are on a second or later course, and ≈1.6 pts of the off-now group restarted once and stopped again, so 5.0+1.6 = 6.6 of 16.5 ever-users = 40% cycled. That fits ~35% one-year persistence and 36–47% restart within a year. Current users ≈ 26.2M of ~265M adults. Ever-use is up only 1.5 pts because few new people are starting. Current use is down 1.1 pts for four reasons: prices stuck at $245–350 cash; the 2027 fracture findings pushing older users off (65+ down from 9% to 8%, 50–64 from 22% to 19%); adherence-gated plans dropping people after missed refills; and people moving to unrecorded imported generics (≈1.3M, counted here as current but under-measured). The income gradient has widened: the top third is at 13.5%, sustained by cash-pay and 'metabolic health' use. Off-drug people: ~17.5M adults who used and stopped, and ~200M who never used, mostly uninsured or bottom-third adults outside the Indiana/Arkansas-type Medicaid programmes. Pediatric: ~0.3% of all under-18s (≈220k), up from ~0.12%, mostly adolescents 12+ on semaglutide; children 8–11 remain rare and skew upper-income. No child in the country has more than ~5 years of exposure.

access.public_coverage: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge extended (Jan 2027) through Dec 2029 on unchanged terms: Medicare pays ~$245/month, $50 copay, same BMI/comorbidity criteria. ≈1.5M beneficiaries use it for obesity: 1.5M × $245 × 12 ≈ $4.4B/yr federal spend, which fits CBO's ≥$35B 2026–34 path. Medicare overall (Part D diabetes plus Bridge) pays ≈20% of incretin fills ≈ 5.2M users, consistent with ~8% of ~61M adults 65+ (4.9M) plus ~0.3M disabled under-65 enrollees. Medicaid pays ≈10% of fills ≈ 2.6M users at the same $245 rate; coverage varies by state, and Indiana and Arkansas 1115 waivers make continued coverage conditional on adherence and weigh-ins.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 60+ generic semaglutide brands, $8–45/month. Canada: generic semaglutide CAD 80–110/month. Brazil, Mexico and Turkey have generics. Generic oral semaglutide is spreading across ~170 countries. US exclusivity still runs to ~2031–32.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Prices stalled: TrumpRx/direct cash is still ~$245–350 injectable and $149 for the starting oral dose. Lilly and Novo cite Section 232 tariff exposure and retatrutide capacity limits, and neither has cut since early 2027. Wegovy list is still $1,349; retatrutide launched at a $1,499 list with no TrumpRx price. Payer mix of ~26.2M users: commercial 45% (11.8M), Medicare 20% (5.2M), Medicaid 10% (2.6M), cash/direct 20% (5.2M), gray/imported 5% (1.3M) = 100%. Compounding is effectively over: the 503B exclusion was finalised in Feb 2027 and 503A sales of copies are under injunction. In its place, mail-order Indian and Canadian generics arrive under the personal-importation gap; FDA seizes some parcels but has not prosecuted individuals. Among employers that cover weight management, ~40% now run 'adherence-gated' PBM programmes (proportion-of-days-covered ≥80% and periodic weight verification), and many tie wellness premium surcharges to BMI or enrolment.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, approved Mar 2028)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema, approved Dec 2026)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: smoking and vaping cessation: phase 3 data (May 2028) show semaglutide added to varenicline/NRT raises 6-month abstinence; sNDA filed, no approval yet; widely prescribed off-label via telehealth and some state quitlines

'metabolic health' / longevity use by people without obesity: low-dose oral semaglutide and Foundayo at $149 cash through longevity clinics and concierge practices; the top income third makes up most of it
alcohol reduction, including employer EAP-referred off-label prescribing
pediatric under-12 use off-label under specialist care
reward/craving reduction for gambling and compulsive shopping, still anecdotal
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. CagriSema was approved Dec 2026, but its uptake is modest because it showed no advantage over tirzepatide. Lilly filed the retatrutide BLA Feb 2027 and it was approved Mar 2028, 13 months after filing even with priority review. Label: 28% mean loss at 80 weeks, up to ~30% in BMI≥35. Supply is allocated, and the label carries a body-composition and bone-health monitoring section. Amycretin's NDA was filed Jun 2028, so no approval before mid-2029. Survodutide was filed Oct 2027 and has a decision due late 2028–early 2029; it is not on the market. MariTide (monthly) is in phase 3 and not on the market. Muscle-preserving adjuncts (bimagrumab combinations) report phase 2 results and are not approved. These are now the most-watched assets in the sector because of the bone and muscle findings. The incretin market is ≈$105B in 2028: volume growth is offset by flat US prices and ex-US generic erosion.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Most common class effect; higher with retatrutide escalation; still the leading cause of discontinuation.
Elevated with rapid weight loss; more salient with ~28% loss agents.
No causal confirmation in long-term data; absolute risk low.

Now recognised as a population problem. In users 65+ on therapy >2 years, a large claims-plus-DEXA cohort finds sarcopenia criteria met roughly 1.5× as often as matched non-users; grip-strength and gait-speed declines reported. Lean-mass share of loss is ~25–40% depending on age and activity.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA class safety communication (Jul 2027) and class label update (2028) recommending baseline body-composition assessment and resistance-training/protein counselling for 65+. Medicare Bridge renewal requires a documented counselling visit.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New in this window. Observational data in 65+ long-term users show hip/vertebral fragility fracture hazard ratios of ~1.3–1.4, concentrated in women and in cycling users with repeated rapid loss. A withheld manufacturer substudy showed BMD declines consistent with this.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class labelling of BMD loss (2028); DEXA recommended before and during long-term use in 65+ and postmenopausal women; Senate HELP investigation into disclosure.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohort studies still conflict; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label for semaglutide; FDA added a warnings-section mention in 2027 without a class determination.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association in EMA, MHRA or systematic-review data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Warning removed from US labels (Jan 2026); unchanged.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Two observational survey studies (2027) report self-rated reduced pleasure in roughly 10–15% of long-term users, with dose dependence. No validated RCT measure. The same mechanism is now being marketed as a benefit for nicotine and alcohol reduction.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None. FDA requested an anhedonia scale in retatrutide postmarketing studies.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Substantial regain within a year in most trial data. Now also driven by adherence-gated coverage cut-offs, which produce abrupt, involuntary stops.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly. Disability advocates challenge abrupt-termination rules in Indiana waiver litigation.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Further observational signals for iron, B12, vitamin D and protein insufficiency, especially in older and high-loss users.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; effects in adolescents who may take these for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About six years of follow-up exist. Bone findings suggest cycling may compound loss; adolescent bone-accrual data are absent.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements; FDA asked for pediatric bone-accrual studies (2028).

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit product harms (dosing errors, contamination)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Compounded reports fell after the 503B exclusion. Harms now come mostly from imported and counterfeit pens; poison-centre calls about mail-order product are rising.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 503B exclusion final (Feb 2027); import alerts; parcel seizures.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Reported in trials; seen in real-world use at a few percent; usually transient.

food_and_beverage.state: Volume pressure continues in snacks, confectionery and sugary drinks, but at roughly 2026 rates rather than accelerating, since current users are slightly down. Protein, fibre and 'bone-health' (calcium, vitamin D) callouts are the new standard claims. Dairy and protein-shake makers are gaining.

alcohol.state: Volumes keep contracting among heavy drinkers. EAP-referred off-label use and the nicotine-cessation coverage add a second 'cravings' cohort. Spirits majors cut forecasts again in 2027. Tobacco and vape makers name GLP-1 cessation use as a risk for the first time in 10-K filings.

restaurants.state: Traffic holds; small plates, protein-forward menus and 'occasion' drinks are standard. Casual-dining buffets and value-volume chains in high-uptake suburbs underperform.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking but stabilise as cycling users regain weight. Mainstream brands stock wider size runs per style because customers' sizes now move both ways.

fitness.state: Growing on the bone and muscle findings: resistance-training studios, DEXA-scan-plus-coaching chains and Medicare Advantage 'strength benefit' partnerships. 'Prescribed lifting' is a product category.

insurance.state: No change in who pays. Employer coverage drifts from 60% to 58%. Adherence gating, BMI-linked wellness surcharges and PBM outcomes contracts are now the cost-control tools. Pharmacy trend is ~+9% because prices are flat and volume is still growing in covered groups.

pharma.state: Lilly widens its lead with retatrutide and Foundayo. Novo Nordisk faces securities suits, a Senate investigation and a CEO change after the bone-data scandal. Flat US prices preserve margins while ex-US revenue erodes under generics. The muscle-preserving-adjunct race is the main deal theme.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Among insured professionals over 40, being on the drug is the default. Stopping is what has to be explained: 'bone scan', 'trying for a baby', 'coverage lapsed'. Visible regain is read as a lapse in coverage or discipline. Leaner arms and a stooped posture in older users are newly noticed as an 'on it too long' look.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The gradient has widened: 13.5% of the top third versus 6.5% of the bottom third. The affluent use low-dose 'metabolic' regimens together with DEXA monitoring and strength coaching. Lower-income users cycle with their coverage, or buy Indian pens online and go without bone monitoring. Locally, among women 45–60 in Dallas–Fort Worth's finance and insurance workforce, office surveys put use at around a third, and pharmacy-adjacent lunch spots sell protein bowls by the gram.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Smaller shared meals, protein first and sweets as ceremony are normal. Holidays and weddings have a hosting etiquette for 'on' and 'off' guests. Family tables split between people who eat and people who graze.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Dating profiles commonly state 'on' or 'off', and some apps offer the filter. Couples where one partner is on and one off report mismatched appetites for food, drink and sometimes sex; this is talked about openly, not quantified.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite of any kind (food, nicotine, alcohol, gambling) is treated as something to manage medically. Not dampening it is starting to be read as a choice.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Survey studies report reduced pleasure in ~10–15% of long-term users, dose-dependent; there is no RCT-grade measure. Employers do not mention blunting, but they reward its observable correlates: fewer sick days, lower EAP alcohol claims, passing sleep-apnea screening, and steady demeanour in performance reviews.
interior_life.framing: Talked about as steadiness. Wellness vendors market 'even-keel' outcomes to HR, and the same effect is called a side effect when users complain and a treatment when it ends smoking or drinking. Clinicians use 'dose-dependent reward modulation'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Adherence and employment are correlated. Trucking fleets steer drivers onto tirzepatide to clear DOT sleep-apnea requirements, and drivers who stop fail recertification. Adherence-gated plans mean missed refills show up in HR-adjacent PBM dashboards. Sales and creative roles quietly lower doses, while logistics, call-centre and compliance roles favour staying on.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Stand-up comics and songwriters joke about 'writing off-dose'. A few musicians publicly schedule drug holidays around touring. Users still gravitate to intense flavours and loud, high-stimulation leisure, and bars sell 'one good drink' experiences.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Reports of reduced desire persist. Some couples time dose days around anniversaries. Sex therapists now ask about incretin dose at intake.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Visible on cost and control, not temperament. The India/Canada price gap is a stump-speech staple. Teamsters and SEIU locals bargain over whether PBM adherence data may reach employers. Disability-rights groups sue over Indiana's waiver. No measurable change in turnout or mood is established, though some commentators speculate about it.

state.regulatory_posture: Still pro-access and pro-speed on approvals (CagriSema, retatrutide), but defensive on safety after the bone findings and the Novo disclosure scandal: class labelling, a Senate HELP investigation, DOJ civil investigative demands. Enforcement against compounders is complete; enforcement against imports is selective.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate. Medicare Bridge extended at $245/$50. TrumpRx cash prices frozen at ~$245–350 and $149 for orals. Medicaid coverage is state by state at $245.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Benefits conditioning is now formal. CMS-approved 1115 waivers in Indiana and Arkansas (Oct 2027) continue Medicaid GLP-1 coverage only with ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered from pharmacy claims and a quarterly verified weigh-in at a pharmacy kiosk or clinic. Miss two checks and coverage ends for 12 months. Several state employee plans and ~40% of covering private employers use similar PBM gating, and federal wellness rules allow BMI-linked premium surcharges of up to 30% of premium.
state.workforce_or_military: No military mandate. DOT sleep-apnea screening makes tirzepatide a de facto job requirement for some commercial drivers. The Army allows GLP-1 use for recruits who meet accession weight standards, which is contested.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The US price stall against $8–45 Indian generics is the visible fact. India's exports to the US by mail are an irritant in trade talks. Section 232 pharma tariffs are cited by manufacturers as the reason prices won't fall. Retatrutide supply is allocated domestically first.

events.event: CMS extends the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge through 2029 on unchanged $245/$50 terms; Lilly and Novo decline further TrumpRx cuts, citing tariff exposure and capacity, and cash prices hold at ~$245–350

A large Medicare claims cohort links more than two years of incretin use in adults 65+ to ~1.3–1.4× fragility-fracture risk and higher sarcopenia rates; FDA issues a class safety communication recommending DEXA and strength counselling

Former Novo Nordisk statistician alleges an internal bone-density substudy in older trial participants was kept out of publications and briefing documents; Novo concedes 'delayed disclosure', its CEO departs, and the Senate HELP Committee opens hearings
CMS approves Indiana and Arkansas Medicaid waivers that cut GLP-1 coverage for enrollees falling below 80% refill adherence or missing quarterly verified weigh-ins; disability advocates sue
FDA approves Lilly's retatrutide, the first triple agonist, at 28–30% mean weight loss; list $1,499 a month, supply allocated, bone and body-composition monitoring written into the label

Phase 3 trial shows semaglutide added to standard therapy raises six-month smoking abstinence; Novo files for the indication while telehealth longevity clinics already prescribe low-dose orals off-label for cessation and 'metabolic health'

open_tensions: Benefits now monitor adherence, and adherence tracks employment, yet the fracture data say long-term continuous use harms older bones. The state and employers are rewarding exactly the exposure the label now warns about.
US prices have stalled at $245–1,499 while generics sell for $8–45 abroad; a growing import gray market brings in unmonitored users, and no one has decided whether to tolerate it or stop it.
The reward-blunting mechanism is being sold as a treatment for nicotine and alcohol and rewarded at work as steadiness, while it remains unmeasured as a harm.
Retatrutide brings surgical-grade weight loss to a population already losing lean mass and bone; muscle-preserving adjuncts are still years from approval.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide exists in the US; exclusivity runs to ~2031–32.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
Medicare pays ~$245 a month with a ~$50 beneficiary copay under the GLP-1 Bridge, on the same BMI/comorbidity criteria.
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still $149–150 a month cash through TrumpRx and manufacturer direct channels.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.

prose.headline: Fewer Americans are on GLP-1s, and the ones who stay are the ones being rewarded: how 'steady' became a job skill
prose.world_in_600_words:
By late 2028 fewer Americans are on incretin drugs than two years ago, about one adult in ten, down from eleven. Yet being on one has never been less remarkable. Among insured professionals over forty, being on the drug is simply the default, and stopping is what needs an explanation. The usual explanations are a bone scan, a pregnancy, or lapsed coverage.

Price explains most of the decline. The steep falls of 2025 and 2026 ended at about $245 to $350 a month for injectables and $149 for oral starting doses. Lilly and Novo point to tariffs and to capacity tied up in Lilly's new drug, retatrutide, and neither has cut again. Wegovy's list price is still $1,349. Retatrutide, approved in March, lists at $1,499 and is allocated by supply. Meanwhile Indian generic semaglutide sells for the price of a takeout lunch, and roughly a million Americans now buy it by mail. Compounded copies were shut down in 2027; imported pens took their place, with no prescriber watching.

The second reason is bones. In mid-2027 a Medicare claims study found that adults over sixty-five on these drugs for more than two years broke hips and vertebrae about a third more often, and met sarcopenia criteria more often, than matched peers. The FDA told doctors to order bone scans and prescribe resistance training. Two months later a former Novo Nordisk statistician said a company substudy showing bone-density loss in older participants had been kept out of publications. Novo called it delayed disclosure. Its chief executive left, and the Senate is holding hearings. Older users came off in visible numbers. Gyms selling a bone scan plus a coaching package opened in strip malls that used to hold mattress stores.

Who pays has not changed: employers, Medicare's extended Bridge programme at $245 with a $50 copay, Medicaid where states choose, and cash. What has changed is what payers ask for in return. About two in five employers that still cover weight management route members through pharmacy-benefit programmes that check refill adherence and require periodic verified weigh-ins. Indiana and Arkansas have written the same rules into Medicaid: miss two refills or two weigh-ins and coverage stops for a year. Trucking fleets steer drivers onto tirzepatide because it treats the sleep apnea that federal screening flags. Adherence and employment now track each other, and nobody planned it.

The drugs' quieting effect on craving, the 'Ozempic personality' of 2026, has not been measured as a harm. Surveys suggest that roughly one long-term user in eight reports less pleasure, more at higher doses. It is being promoted as a cure: a May trial showed semaglutide helping smokers quit, and longevity clinics in Scottsdale and Austin already prescribe low-dose pills for 'metabolic health' to people who were never heavy. HR departments see fewer sick days and fewer alcohol claims and call it steadiness. Comedians joke about writing off-dose. Unions are negotiating whether refill data can ever reach a supervisor.

In Dallas–Fort Worth's insurance and banking offices, about a third of women between forty-five and sixty are on a drug, and lunch places sell protein by the gram. In Gary, Indiana, people schedule their lives around a pharmacy-kiosk scale. Snack makers have adapted and spirits makers keep contracting. Plus-size retailers have stabilised, partly because cycling users keep regaining weight. On the surface the country looks fine. The open question is whether the institutions now rewarding people for staying on these drugs have read the new bone warnings on the label.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Rochelle Banks wakes at 5:10 in Gary, Indiana, and checks the pharmacy app before her coffee. Green bar: 94 percent adherence. Weigh-in due Friday. She is fifty-two, a home health aide, and on Zepbound through the state's Medicaid plan.

Her first client is Mr. Okafor, eighty-one. She helps him stand the way the physical therapist showed her, hands under the elbows, count of three. He was on Ozempic for six years and stopped after the hip. He asks whether she lifts. She says she carries people all day. He says that's not the same.

At lunch she eats half a turkey wrap in the car and saves the other half, the way she always does now. Her daughter Kiara texts a photo of a box from Hyderabad: three pens, forty-one dollars. Rochelle types don't, deletes it, types be careful, sends that.

At three a supervisor calls about next month's schedule. The agency likes her. Reliable, he says. Never a sick day.

She stops at the CVS on Broadway because Friday is a double shift. The kiosk asks for her Medicaid ID and a photo. She takes off her shoes. The scale reads, the screen says Verified, and a receipt prints with a QR code she will never scan.

At home Darnell is frying fish. He stopped last spring when the plan dropped him for missing a refill during his brother's funeral, and he's heavier now and happier, she thinks, or louder. He offers her a piece. She takes one, eats it slowly, and finds she can't quite remember whether she used to love this or just used to want it.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Phase 3 trial shows semaglutide added to standard therapy raises six-month smoking abstinence; Novo files for the indication
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: nicotine use was only anecdotal and observational in 2026, yet a phase 3 with a six-month endpoint reads out and the sNDA is filed in the same month, which is implausibly fast with no phase 2 or trial-start chain shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Trucking fleets steer drivers onto tirzepatide to clear DOT sleep-apnea requirements, and drivers who stop fail recertification.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: DOT has no hard sleep-apnea standard and CPAP is the usual route to clearance, so a de facto tirzepatide requirement with recertification failures within two years is asserted without a chain.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Medicare Bridge renewal requires a documented counselling visit.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: the Bridge was extended in Jan 2027 'on unchanged terms', before the Jul 2027 safety communication, so a counselling condition on renewal contradicts the world's own timeline and 'same criteria' claims.

rationale.badness: The state and employers condition coverage on adherence and weigh-ins (Indiana/Arkansas waivers, ~40% PBM gating, BMI-linked surcharges), so people are pressured to stay on a drug whose label now warns about bone loss; autonomy is the worst dimension. Inequality widens (13.5% vs 6.5%), the fracture and sarcopenia findings add a real health ledger, and blunting is unmeasured while being rewarded at work. Falling use and normalisation keep this a harder society with new losers rather than a catastrophe, so it sits in the 6–7 band.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is visibly realised and traceable to events: -1.1pp (9.9%), stalled prices, status-quo coverage, nicotine and longevity use, the muscle/bone wave, retatrutide, the Novo scandal, normalisation, Medicaid conditioning and employer-encouraged personality layer. Employer gating stretches 'status_quo' only slightly. mechanism: Several changes are asserted rather than shown. The nicotine phase 3 plus filing is too fast, the trucking/DOT claim has no chain, the counselling requirement contradicts the 'unchanged terms' extension, and 'Price explains most of the decline' is odd when prices merely stalled. The prose also has Darnell dropped for one missed refill, against a 'two misses' rule. magnitude: On-drug 9.9% and ever-used 16.5% are inside the envelope, the retatrutide, CagriSema, amycretin and survodutide timings obey the approval rules, and the payer mix, Medicare 5.2M users and $4.4B arithmetic reconcile. Small gaps remain: '~200M never used' versus about 221M implied, and age bands that weight to ~10.4% rather than 9.9%.
rationale.generativity: The Rochelle scene is full of concrete texture: the adherence bar, the kiosk scale and photo, the Hyderabad pens, Mr. Okafor's remark about lifting, and Darnell's lapse. Implied scenes abound, including the HR dashboards, union bargaining, the DFW lunch spots, the strip-mall DEXA gyms and dating filters. It shows more than it explains, though the prose preamble does some explaining.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Among insured professionals over 40, being on the drug is the default.
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails magnitude. 'Default' implies a majority, but the world's own figures put the top income third at 13.5% and ages 30–49 at 10% and 50–64 at 19%. A majority of insured professionals over 40 on the drug cannot sit alongside those figures.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Price explains most of the decline.
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails mechanism. The stalled-price driver means prices stopped falling, which does not remove users. The world note lists four causes (price, fractures, adherence gating, imports) and does not rank price first, and employer coverage fell only 2 points.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Trucking fleets steer drivers onto tirzepatide to clear DOT sleep-apnea requirements, and drivers who stop fail recertification.
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails mechanism. It asserts a federal sleep-apnea screening regime and a recertification failure chain that the parent world does not support. The step from stopping the drug to failing recertification is not shown.

rationale.badness: Benefits conditioning in Indiana and Arkansas (80% proportion-of-days-covered, kiosk weigh-ins, 12-month loss of coverage) and adherence data reaching HR dashboards push people toward the exposure the bone label warns about. That is structural, normalised and hard to see from inside, which is why autonomy scores highest. Inequality widens (13.5% vs 6.5%, unmonitored imported pens for lower-income users) and the harm of reward blunting stays unmeasured. Nothing is melodramatic beyond the stipulated scandal, so overall stays at a recognisably harder society rather than a refuse-to-live-in one.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is realised and traceable to events and fields: adoption -1.1, stalled prices, status-quo coverage, nicotine and longevity use, the bone and muscle wave, retatrutide, the Novo scandal, conditioning, and employer encouragement. The Medicare counselling requirement is a minor tweak to status quo. mechanism: Several links are asserted or contradictory. 'Price explains most of the decline' conflicts with the four-cause note and with a price stall; the DOT recertification chain is unsupported; the 'default' claim has no basis. The 50–64 decline is blamed on fractures that are measured in 65+ users. magnitude: The figures sit inside the envelope and reconcile closely: 9.9% and 16.5%, 26.2M users, a payer mix summing to 100%, Medicare 5.2M against 8% of 61M, and $4.4B for 1.5M × $245 × 12. The retatrutide approval comes 13 months after filing, which the approval rules allow. Minor gaps remain: '~200M never used' against about 221M, and the 'default' overstatement.
rationale.generativity: The Rochelle Banks day is concrete: the adherence app, the kiosk weigh-in with shoes off, the Hyderabad pens, Mr. Okafor's hip, and Darnell's lapsed coverage. The world also implies other characters, such as truckers, HR analysts, union reps, sex therapists, and longevity-clinic patients, and it carries local texture like the Dallas–Fort Worth lunch spots and the strip-mall bone-scan gyms. Little of it is left merely explained.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Trucking fleets steer drivers onto tirzepatide to clear DOT sleep-apnea requirements, and drivers who stop fail recertification.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: DOT has no formal OSA treatment mandate that tirzepatide satisfies, and CPAP remains the standard route. The claim that stopping the drug makes a driver fail recertification is asserted, with no regulatory chain shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Amycretin's NDA was filed Jun 2028, so no approval before mid-2029.
least_plausible_claims.why: magnitude: amycretin entered phase 3 in May 2026, and an NDA 25 months later leaves no room for enrollment, a 70-80 week obesity trial and analysis. The filing is also not listed in `events`, which the envelope requires when no filing was stated at the start.

least_plausible_claims.quote: He stopped last spring when the plan dropped him for missing a refill during his brother's funeral
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: the world and article say the waiver ends coverage only after two missed checks or refills, or adherence below 80%. A single missed refill triggering a 12-month cutoff contradicts that rule.

rationale.badness: Benefits conditioning couples Medicaid and employer coverage to refill adherence and weigh-ins, and adherence tracks employment (interior_life/effect_on_work, state/conditioning_or_surveillance). Abrupt involuntary stops raise regain and cycling, which the bone data tie to harm. The top third (13.5%) versus bottom third (6.5%) widens the access gap, with bottom-third users buying unmonitored imported pens. Reward blunting in 10-15% of long-term users is rewarded as 'steadiness' and not measured as a harm, which weakens people's ability to name what is happening to them. This is a recognisably harder society with new losers, not a collapse.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Phase 3 trial shows semaglutide added to standard therapy raises six-month smoking abstinence; Novo files for the indication
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: nicotine use was only anecdotal and observational in 2026, yet a phase 3 with a six-month endpoint reads out and the sNDA is filed in the same month, which is implausibly fast with no phase 2 or trial-start chain shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Trucking fleets steer drivers onto tirzepatide to clear DOT sleep-apnea requirements, and drivers who stop fail recertification.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: DOT has no hard sleep-apnea standard and CPAP is the usual route to clearance, so a de facto tirzepatide requirement with recertification failures within two years is asserted without a chain.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Medicare Bridge renewal requires a documented counselling visit.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: the Bridge was extended in Jan 2027 'on unchanged terms', before the Jul 2027 safety communication, so a counselling condition on renewal contradicts the world's own timeline and 'same criteria' claims.

rationale.badness: The state and employers condition coverage on adherence and weigh-ins (Indiana/Arkansas waivers, ~40% PBM gating, BMI-linked surcharges), so people are pressured to stay on a drug whose label now warns about bone loss; autonomy is the worst dimension. Inequality widens (13.5% vs 6.5%), the fracture and sarcopenia findings add a real health ledger, and blunting is unmeasured while being rewarded at work. Falling use and normalisation keep this a harder society with new losers rather than a catastrophe, so it sits in the 6–7 band.
